resolution_reason: Both of us put ambiguous because they mention overpaying a balance and a servicer, but  never say what kind of loan or account it is.
Narrative just says "he wouldn't loan me money" because of discrimination, but we have absolutely zero clue what kind of loan it was for.
They just said "card" was stolen for chime. We could not agree if it was a bank account or ambiguous since it didn't specify debit/credit, so we just scrapped it.

This one was super confusing. It mentions an 'account', a 'card' and 'no existing loans', but never says whether it's a bank account, a credit card or some kind of loan app. Since we couldn't tell which team would handle it without guessing, we removed it.

They talk about a 'fairly new loan' with late fees and wrong late payments on their credit report, but we have no clue if it's a car loan, personal loan or even a mortgage. We didn't want to just default to Consumer loan, so we removed it.

Both of us marked this ambiguous. The customer disputes charges from places they've never been, but never says if it's a credit card, a debit card or something else, and no company is named either. Rule 5 says we can't assume the card type, so we removed it.

A said Debt collection and B said Credit reporting, and both make some sense. But the ticket is super short, we don't know what the 'service' was, and we can't tell whether they're complaining about the company chasing them or about the credit report. We couldn't agree on a primary complaint, so we removed it.

This one asks for 'verification of this debt' on an account they don't recognise, but it doesn't say who they're dealing with (a collector, a bank or a credit bureau) or what kind of account it is. We felt there wasn't enough to go on, so we removed it.

Both of us were only Medium on this one. It's an unauthorized $82 charge that got denied, but they never say if it was on a bank account, a credit card, a debit card or a payment app. We couldn't tell which team would handle it, so we removed it.

A said Credit card and B said Bank account. Key Bank gave a $59 credit for an item that never arrived and then reversed it, but the customer never says if the payment was made with a credit card, a debit card or from their account. We couldn't decide without guessing, so we removed it.

Both of us marked this ambiguous. The customer closed all their Capital One accounts and is just annoyed about unsolicited emails. There's no product problem and no debt being collected, so it doesn't fit any of our categories and we removed it.
Both of us marked this ambiguous. The customer is asking for an affordable payment plan, but there's zero info on what the account is (credit card, loan, mortgage, etc.), so we removed it.
This one is about payments to TIAA not being forwarded after the loan was sold, but it never says what kind of loan it is. It could easily be a mortgage, so we didn't want to guess and removed it.

This one was confusing. Wells Fargo didn't honour a stop payment on a car rental purchase, but the customer only says 'card numbers' and 'my account' without saying if it's a debit or credit card. Since that changes the category (Rule 5), we removed it.
Barely readable. Something about retail store "shield credit protection" insurance. Does not fit in any labels.
